content.title: Louisville vs Michigan State score today, NCAA Tournament highlights
content.text: Updated March 21, 2026, 10:46 p.m. ETBUFFALO, NY — One day removed from his first NCAA Tournament win as a head coach, on the cusp of Louisville basketball's first trip to the Sweet 16 in more than a decade, Pat Kelsey kept his eyes on the process."It's not the destination, it's the journey," he said Friday. "That's what fires me up."The next step of the journey will play out on the biggest stage of his career. His sixth-seeded Cardinals are set to face No. 3-seed Michigan State today at KeyBank Center with a spot in the second weekend of March Madness at stake. Tipoff is set for approximately 2:45 p.m.The winner will advance to next week's East Regional, which begins March 27 at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. The opponent will be either No. 2 UConn or No. 7 UCLA.UofL is coming off its first win in the Big Dance since 2017, 83-79 over No. 11 South Florida on Thursday. It led for more than 35 minutes and by as many as 23 points (with seven minutes and change on the clock in the second half) but let the Bulls pull within single digits for the final 5:24."We have a bunch of guys who had the resolve and the wherewithal and the toughness to figure out a way to advance in this tournament," Kelsey said afterward.Tom Izzo's Spartans are pretty tough, too. They're coming off a 92-67 rout of No. 14 North Dakota State on Thursday and are led by a second-team All-American in redshirt sophomore point guard Jeremy Fears Jr., who averages a team-high 15.4 points and a Division I-leading 9.2 assists per game.Louisville will be without its PG1, projected NBA lottery pick Mikel Brown Jr., for a sixth consecutive game due to a lower back injury.The Cards haven't played MSU since Dec. 1, 2021: a 73-64 loss in East Lansing, Michigan. The last meeting between the programs in the Big Dance was an Elite Eight overtime thriller in 2015 — also won by the Spartans, 76-70.Follow along with live updates from KeyBank Center below:Ryan Conwell on Louisville basketball's season-ending loss to Michigan State in NCAA TournamentHere's what Ryan Conwell had to say after his collegiate career came to an end with Louisville's loss to MIchigan State in the NCAA Tournament's Round of 32:Mikel Brown Jr. reflects after Louisville basketball season ends in NCAA TournamentHere's what Mikel Brown Jr., who missed the final six games of the season due to a reaggravated back injury, had to say about UofL fell to Michigan State:FINAL | Michigan State 77, Louisville 694:23 2H | Michigan State 66, Louisville 56The Spartans used a flagrant 1 foul call on Vangelis Zougris to score a five-point possession that may have broke the game open for good. UofL faced its biggest deficit at 66-53 after the call.10:17 2H | Michigan State 53, Louisville 47UofL has trailed for 25 plus minutes, but had a chance to tie the game at 50 on an Aly Khalifa 3-pointer. His miss led to a basket for the Spartans, but the Cards are staying within striking distance.15:51, 2H | Michigan State 42, Louisville 37The Cards withstood an early spurt of six straight points and have now held the Spartans scoreless the last 2:28 minutes. UofL has continued to cause havoc defensively, forcing Sparty into three turnovers to make their total 12 for the game.HALF | Michigan State 36, Louisville 31It ... could be a lot worse for the Cards, who trailed the Spartans by as many as 10 points, 22-12, with 9:46 to play in the half. They've kept it close by forcing nine turnovers — and a 16-10 edge in paint scoring.UofL's Ryan Conwell and Adrian Wooley all scorers with nine points apiece during the opening 20 minutes.Two big questions heading into the second half: Will MSU keep shooting 50% from 3? Can Louisville bounce back from a 4-for-18 showing from beyond the arc?3:46, 1H | Michigan State 31, Louisville 23Crucial sequence just before the timeout: His team trailing 27-23, Adrian Wooley passed up a spacious lane to the basket and instead dished to an open Kobe Rodgers standing beyond the arc in the right corner. Rodgers missed and, at the other end, fouled Spartans guard Trey Fort as he knocked down a 3.Fort converted the 4-point play.7:06, 1H | Michigan State 27, Louisville 19The Spartans are just operating at a higher level offensively right now: 10 for 19, 5 for 8 from 3.Entering today, Izzo's team was averaging 7.7 triples per game.The Cards are 7 for 22 and 3 for 14, respectively.11:55, 1H | Michigan State 19, Louisville 12The Spartans have started to create some separation. They entered the timeout having made four shots in a row — the last two coming from Jaxon Kohler.The Cards, on the other hand, are 1 for their last 8 from the field. They've started 2 for 10 from 3-point range.UofL's leading scorer, Ryan Conwell, hit the bench at the 15:43 mark after picking up two early fouls.15:43, 1H | Louisville 7, Michigan State 7We're all knotted up after the first segment.Vangelis Zougris leads the Cards with four points, while Coen Carr is pacing the Spartans with five.UofL jumped out to a 4-0 lead behind Zougris' back-to-back buckets in the paint.Starting lineups | Louisville vs Michigan StateStarting for the Cards:G Adrian WooleyG Isaac McKneelyG Ryan ConwellF J'Vonne HadleyC Vangelis ZougrisStarting for the Spartans:G Jeremy Fears Jr.G Jordan ScottF Jaxon KohlerF Coen CarrC Carson CooperLouisville vs Michigan State pick: The Courier Journal's March Madness Round of 32 predictionClick here to see who The Courier Journal's Brooks Holton is taking in the second-round matchup.Can Louisville basketball outtough Michigan State to reach NCAA Tournament's Sweet 16?Standing between Louisville and its first Sweet 16 in 11 years: the exact type of team that’s given it fits all season. Can the Cards outtough Michigan State? They certainly can’t let the past define them.“You don’t want to regret anything," Sananda Fru told The Courier Journal.Click here to read more.Catching up with Louisville native, ex-Card Kaleb Glenn before UofL faces Michigan State in March MadnessThe Courier Journal spoke with 502 native/former UofL forward Kaleb Glenn ahead of a surreal Round of 32 game between his old/hometown team and his new one, Michigan State.“I wish I wasn't hurt so I could be out there," Glenn said.Click here to read more.C.L.
